summary: The 13th Dalai Lama (1876–1933) worked in Buddhist studies, Tibetology, and religious studies. He studied under teachers including Agvan Dorzhiev, Tertön Sogyal, Pa Ri Rabsal, and Jampa Gyatso, and taught numerous students, including Rangjung Rigpe Dorje.

16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje (1924–1981) worked in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Kalu Rinpoche, the 1st Beru Khyentse, and Tulku Urgyen Rinpoche, and taught numerous students, including Reginald A. Ray and Joseph Goldstein.
19th Kushok Bakula Rinpoche (1917–2003) was active in Buddhist studies and Tibetology. He studied under Ngawang Lobzang Gyatso, Khangsar Dorje Chang, and Jamphel Yeshe Gyaltsen.

Active in Tibetology and Buddhist studies, 2nd Beru Khyentse (born 1947) studied under Dzongsar Khenpo Chimey Rinpoche, Kalu Rinpoche, the 16th Karmapa Rangjung Rigpe Dorje, Khunu Lama Tenzin Gyaltsen, Sakya Trizin Ngawang Kunga, and Dilgo Khyentse.
A Drö Khenpo Yeshe Gyatso studied under Jamgon Ju Mipham Gyatso and Khenpo Shenga.

A. A. Krishnaswami Ayyangar (1892–1953) worked in Indology. He studied at Pachaiyappa's College (~1908–1911), where he also held a post (1911–1918), before serving as a professor at the University of Mysore (1918–1947).

A. Aiyappan (1905–1988) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He studied at the University of Madras (~1923–1927), served as Superintendent at the Government Museum, Chennai (~1940–1960), and held a post at the University of Kerala (~1969–1971).
Active in Indology and philosophy, A. Anantacharya served as a Pandit at the Mysore Archaeological Department and as head of the Yatiraja Mutt (attested 1926).

Specializing in Indology, A. B. Gajendragadkar served as a Senior Dakshina Fellow at Deccan College Post-Graduate and Research Institute and as a lecturer on Sanskrit at Karnatak Arts College, Dharwad.

A. Charles Muller (born 1953) works in Buddhist studies, Sinology, and Japanology. He earned his Ph.D. at Stony Brook University under Sung Bae Park and held posts at Toyo Gakuen University, the University of Tokyo, and Musashino University.
A. G. Mohan (born 1945) is a scholar in Indology and religious studies. He studied under Tirumalai Krishnamacharya from ~1971 to 1989 and founded the Krishnamacharya Yoga Mandiram in 1976.

A. H. Armstrong (1909–1997) was a philosopher who studied at Jesus College, Cambridge. He held academic posts at Swansea, the University of Malta, Beaumont College, Cardiff University, and served as Gladstone Professor of Greek at the University of Liverpool (1950–1972).

Awadh Kishore Narain (1925–2013) worked in Indology, history, archaeology, and Buddhist studies. He studied at Banaras Hindu University and SOAS under Arthur Llewellyn Basham, and was later a professor at the University of Wisconsin-Madison (1971–1987).

A. K. Ramanujan (1929–1993) worked in linguistics and Indology, studying at Maharaja's College, Mysore, the University of Mysore, and Indiana University. He taught at Maharaja Sayajirao University of Baroda and was a professor at the University of Chicago from 1962.
A. M. D'Rozario worked in Tibetology and other fields. He completed an M.Sc. at the University of Allahabad and earned a Ph.D. at the University of Cambridge.

A. Mahadeva Sastri (1861–1926) worked in Indology and philosophy. He served as Curator at the Oriental Research Institute Mysore (~1891–1916) and Director at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (~1916–1926).

A scholar of Indology, A. N. Krishna Aiyangar studied under K. V. Rangaswami Aiyangar. He served as Joint Editor of Brahmavidya at the Adyar Library and Research Centre (attested 1940–1950) and as Librarian at the National Archives of India (attested 1954).

A. N. Narasimhia worked in linguistics and Indology. He completed a PhD at SOAS University of London under Ralph Lilley Turner (~1930–1933) and held posts at Maharaja's College, Mysore, and the University of Mysore around 1934.
A. P. Buddhadatta (1887–1962) was a scholar in Buddhist studies and Indology. He served as a tutor in Pali at Ananda College and was a member of Kalyanavamsa Nikaya (attested 1923).

A. S. Ramanatha Ayyar (died 1941) worked in history, archaeology, and Indology. He served as Epigraphical Assistant at the Archaeological Survey of India (1918–1941) and Superintendent of the Department of Archaeology, Travancore State (1922).
